entries.title: Rutaecarpine Protects against Acetaminophen-Induced Acute Liver Injury in Mice by Activating Antioxidant Enzymes

sentences: The induction of CYP2E1 alongside HMOX1 is mechanistically coherent with reactive oxygen species generation during halogenated aromatic metabolism, which may trigger downstream heme oxygenase-mediated cytoprotection [1][2].

CYP2E1, supported by 14 publications, is a well-characterized mediator of halogenated compound bioactivation; its induction is consistent with oxidative metabolite generation and has been linked to downstream HMOX1 co-induction in models of chemical hepatotoxicity [1][5].

Confidence in the mechanistic interpretation of the 1,2-DCB cardiac transcriptomic response is highest for the oxidative stress and xenobiotic metabolism signatures, which are supported by multiple consensus genes (HMOX1, CYP2E1, SRXN1, TXNRD1) with strong cross-study literature concordance [3][4][1].
The upregulation of canonical NRF2 target genes NQO1 and GCLC is consistent with an adaptive cellular response to electrophilic or oxidative insult generated during 1,2-DCB biotransformation [1].
The liver enrichment is consistent with the known hepatic biotransformation of 1,2-DCB via CYP2E1 and the shared phase II detoxification machinery between liver and kidney [16][1].

Both genes are well-established indicators of electrophilic and oxidative stress-driven NRF2 activation, and their upregulation in the kidney is consistent with the biotransformation of 1,2-DCB to reactive intermediates capable of activating the KEAP1/NRF2 axis [1][4].

Confidence in the biological interpretation of the 1,2-DCB renal transcriptomic response is high for the NRF2-mediated oxidative stress and xenobiotic metabolism signatures, given the convergent evidence from pathway enrichment, GO term analysis, BMD ordering, and the extensive multi-study literature support for NQO1, GCLC, SRXN1, CYP2E1, CAT, and BAX as consensus response genes [3][1][19].

CYP2E1, a cytochrome P450 isoform known to bioactivate halogenated aromatic compounds and generate reactive oxygen species, was upregulated and appeared in the metabolic and arachidonic acid metabolism pathways; its induction is mechanistically plausible given the role of CYP2E1 in the oxidative metabolism of chlorinated benzenes [1].

statements: Rutaecarpine protects against acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury in mice by activating antioxidant enzymes
Rutaecarpine pretreatment decreases serum ALT/AST activities and hepatic malondialdehyde content, prevents glutathione depletion, inhibits CYP2E1 expression, and reduces inflammatory cytokines

entries.title: Heteromeric complex formation between human cytochrome P450 CYP1A1 and heme oxygenase-1.

sentences: The induction of CYP2E1 alongside HMOX1 is mechanistically coherent with reactive oxygen species generation during halogenated aromatic metabolism, which may trigger downstream heme oxygenase-mediated cytoprotection [1][2].

POR, which encodes NADPH-cytochrome P450 oxidoreductase, was also responsive and has been shown to catalyze lipid peroxidation during ferroptotic cell death [6], and its co-expression with HMOX1 in the context of CYP450 complex formation [2] suggests potential for amplified oxidative injury in cardiac tissue.

statements: CYP1A1 forms a stable complex with HO-1 that is further stabilized in the presence of POR.
The interaction between CYP1A1 and HO-1 affects their functional characteristics, altering Km values but not Vmaxapp.

entries.title: Biomarkers of NRF2 signalling: Current status and future challenges

sentences: Concurrently, response to xenobiotic stimulus (GO:0009410; FDR = 8.90 × 10⁻⁵) was enriched across 15 genes including CYP2E1, HMOX1, MGST1, TXNRD1, and SRXN1, the majority of which were upregulated, consistent with activation of the NRF2 antioxidant response pathway [3][4].

Organ signature analysis indicated that the cardiac gene expression profile bore greatest resemblance to signatures from hepatic Kupffer cells, monocytes/macrophages, and renal tubular epithelium, driven predominantly by HMOX1 enrichment, which is consistent with the known broad inducibility of heme oxygenase-1 across stress-responsive cell types [3].

HMOX1 upregulation is a well-established indicator of NRF2 pathway activation and oxidative stress, and HMOX1, SRXN1, and TXNRD1 have been identified as robust NRF2 activity biomarkers across multiple cell types [3][4].

Confidence in the mechanistic interpretation of the 1,2-DCB cardiac transcriptomic response is highest for the oxidative stress and xenobiotic metabolism signatures, which are supported by multiple consensus genes (HMOX1, CYP2E1, SRXN1, TXNRD1) with strong cross-study literature concordance [3][4][1].
Key NRF2-associated genes — GCLC, NQO1, SRXN1, GPX3, and CAT — were represented across these terms, consistent with activation of the NRF2/ARE antioxidant response pathway [3].

Among the individual dose-responsive genes, NQO1 and GCLC emerged as the most sensitive and biologically informative markers of 1,2-DCB renal exposure, with BMD values at the lower end of the observed range and strong literature support as canonical NRF2 pathway biomarkers across multiple cell types and tissues [3][17].
SRXN1, a sulfiredoxin and additional NRF2 target, was also among the responsive genes, further supporting engagement of the antioxidant response program [3][18].

Confidence in the biological interpretation of the 1,2-DCB renal transcriptomic response is high for the NRF2-mediated oxidative stress and xenobiotic metabolism signatures, given the convergent evidence from pathway enrichment, GO term analysis, BMD ordering, and the extensive multi-study literature support for NQO1, GCLC, SRXN1, CYP2E1, CAT, and BAX as consensus response genes [3][1][19].

The ferroptosis pathway was represented by a complete five-gene set (GCLC, GCLM, GPX4, HMOX1, TP53), all upregulated, consistent with an adaptive cytoprotective response to lipid peroxidation stress [3].

These genes were upregulated across a BMD range of approximately 134–241 ppm and are well-established transcriptional targets of KEAP1-NRF2 signaling activated by electrophilic and oxidative insults [3].

GCLC, GCLM, HMOX1, NQO1, SRXN1, and TXNRD1 have been validated as robust NRF2 activity biomarkers across multiple cell types and species [3, 4], lending high confidence to the interpretation that 1,2-DCB activates hepatic NRF2 signaling in a dose-dependent manner.

GPX4, a phospholipid hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase critical for suppressing ferroptosis, was upregulated with a BMD within the ferroptosis pathway cluster (median ~165 ppm), and its co-induction with GCLC, GCLM, and HMOX1 suggests that lipid peroxidation is an early hepatic stress signal following 1,2-DCB exposure [3].

The predominant upregulation of genes within these pathways — particularly the NRF2-associated antioxidant response genes GCLC, NQO1, SRXN1, and TXNRD1 — is consistent with an adaptive cellular response to oxidative stress induced by 1,2-DCB metabolism [3].

NQO1, a well-established NRF2 target gene and robust biomarker of NRF2 pathway activation across multiple cell types [3], was similarly upregulated and co-enriched with GCLC, SRXN1, and TXNRD1 across multiple GO terms and pathways, collectively constituting a canonical NRF2 transcriptional signature [3, 4].

statements: GCLC, GCLM, HMOX1, NQO1, SRXN1 and TXNRD1 are robust markers for NRF2 activity across multiple cell types.
There is a need for consensus on the most relevant set of genes/proteins that best represent NRF2 activity in different contexts.

entries.title: Binankadsurin A from Kadsura coccinea Fruits Ameliorates Acetaminophen-Induced Liver Injury Through Inhibiting Oxidative Stress by Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 Pathway

sentences: CYP2E1, supported by 14 publications, is a well-characterized mediator of halogenated compound bioactivation; its induction is consistent with oxidative metabolite generation and has been linked to downstream HMOX1 co-induction in models of chemical hepatotoxicity [1][5].

statements: Binankadsurin A (BKA) reduces acetaminophen-induced acute liver damage by inhibiting oxidative stress through activation of the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway.
Pretreatment with BKA mitigates liver injury and improves CYP2E1 expression in mouse livers.
